solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Oncology nerd is confused about one branch of physiology

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece, as a fence goes about a field
the letters of the two words are jumbled, as a confused person's thoughts are

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A muddled cancer specialist gets the wrong end of the stick about a field of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is confused' jumbles ONCOLOGY NERD and 'about' wraps those letters around I.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of hormones and the glands secreting them is a recognised subdivision of human physiology.

clue.text: Preserve former electric vehicle, topless car built outside LA

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former, as in ex-wife
a tram is a vehicle run on electricity from overhead wires

indicators.note: the car loses its top, the first letter in a down light

parts.note: the word car itself, beheaded

indicators.note: the word for built goes around the two letters given, one placed outside the other

parts.note: built means made, constructed

explanation.surface: A tram and a cut-down car are put together near Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the first letter of the car; 'outside' wraps the word for built round LA. Extra marmalade has a higher fruit content.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit preserves include marmalade, and this premium kind contains more fruit than the standard jar.

clue.text: Pot from southern US states

definitions.meaning: a large iron cooking pot used by soldiers in camp
the informal name for the states of the old Confederacy

explanation.surface: A cooking vessel from the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: The army kettle shares its name with the nickname for the American South, from the song Dixie.

clue.text: Am I not able to prize open-ended support?

parts.note: am I not able? contracts to can't I?
to prize (prise) something open is to lever it

explanation.surface: Someone frets that they cannot force open some support or bracket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize' is an accepted spelling of prise, to force open.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam fixed at only one end, as on a balcony or bridge arm, supports a load while its far end is free.

clue.text: Sind badly disrupted by conflict moving to the centre

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are broken open by the next piece pushed into them
the letters of Sind are put together badly, out of order

parts.note: conflict means war

explanation.surface: A Pakistani province is torn apart by fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' jumbles the province's letters and 'disrupted by' pushes the conflict word inside them. Sind is a province of Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards the middle, rather than outwards, is travelling in the inner direction.

clue.text: Just taking off hot record for dance

indicators.note: a letter is taken off the word for just

parts.note: just means fair, honest
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A fair-minded DJ removes a steamy record before the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' removes H from HONEST to leave ONEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick ballroom dance popular in the early twentieth century, taken one pace per beat.

clue.text: Unctuous and cunning when wife's over

indicators.note: when signals the swap: the letter for wife is exchanged for the letter for over

parts.note: cunning means wily
W is the abbreviation for wife
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A smarmy, crafty man behaves once his wife has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the other way: the answer becomes the word for cunning when W takes over from O.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smarmy and ingratiating is greasy in manner, slippery like oil.

clue.text: In short, what could be railway operating every month

indicators.note: in short says the first word of the answer is to be abbreviated, giving YR

parts.note: RY, the short form of railway, is what YR gives when the second word of the answer, round, turns it back to front

explanation.surface: A rail service that runs all the time, abbreviated.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay. YR shortens year, and turning it round gives RY, the abbreviation for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available in all twelve months, not just a season, is open throughout the whole calendar.

clue.text: Go with crew to record how ministries are structured

parts.note: to go is to depart
a crew is a body of men
a tally is a running record or count

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave with a team and log something, in a civil service setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministries are organised into separate divisions, each one a department, so they are arranged by division.

clue.text: Poison in canned beef

indicators.note: in places the beef inside the container

parts.note: canned suggests a tin, the can that holds it
an ox is a beef animal

explanation.surface: Tinned meat has gone off and is poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison produced by a living organism, such as botulinum in spoilt cans.

clue.text: Significant distance for vehicle with slope underneath

parts.note: to heel is to lean or slope over, as a ship does
the base is what lies underneath

explanation.surface: A car's length on a hill matters for how it handles.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap between front and rear axles is a key measurement for any car or lorry.

clue.text: A pal around Oriel, struggling to improve

indicators.note: the word for pal goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a pal is a mate

indicators.note: struggling letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A friend surrounds an Oxford college that is battling to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is an Oxford college; 'struggling' jumbles it and 'around' sets the pal word round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a bad situation better is a formal synonym for improving it.

clue.text: Song musician at first cut from role in West Side Story

indicators.note: that letter is cut from the role's name

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of the musical

indicators.note: only the opening letter of musician is meant

explanation.surface: A song is dropped from the part in a famous musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo number is a type of song.

clue.text: One looks for mine to do well without time in company

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for do well surrounds the rest

parts.note: to prosper is to do well

indicators.note: the time letter goes in the company letters

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a good career and a company to join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' carries its old sense of outside, not lacking: the do-well word wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone searching the ground for gold or ore hopes to find a seam worth digging.

clue.text: What appears on disc of Mozart produced in Australia

definitions.text: What appears on disc of Mozart

indicators.note: the word for produced sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: produced means made

explanation.surface: A Mozart recording pressed down under.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer's middle name is printed on his record labels, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.

clue.text: Dispatch worker maybe with commercial furniture item

parts.note: a commercial is an advert, an ad
a dresser is a piece of furniture with shelves

explanation.surface: A worker in the dispatch room alongside an advert for a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who writes destinations on mail before posting is one who labels it; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: American stalls in Quebec during break

indicators.note: the province name sits within the break, as during a pause

parts.note: to break apart is to part
QUE is a short form of the province Quebec

explanation.surface: Americans holiday in Quebec at intermission.
explanation.definitionFit: In US theatres the ground-floor seating is called by this name, the British term being stalls.

clue.text: Great anger with object returned in bulk

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the word for bulk

parts.note: bulk means mass

indicators.note: the word for object is read back to front

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Fury when an item comes back in a large consignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns END into DNE, which goes 'in' MASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme rage is a kind of insanity, as in being mad with anger.

clue.text: Accept opening with church

parts.note: a stoma is an opening, a pore or a surgical aperture

explanation.surface: A church agrees to an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with or tolerate something is to bear it.

clue.text: Rest live outside university

indicators.note: the word for live goes outside the letter

parts.note: to live somewhere is to reside

explanation.surface: A student takes a break, living off campus.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains after the rest has gone is the remainder or leftovers.

clue.text: In a poor state getting bad wound in the navy

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits in the abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: bad shows the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor in rough shape with a nasty injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns WOUND into UNDOW, which goes 'in' RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shabby, neglected or exhausted is dilapidated.

clue.text: Right to remain head of negotiations

parts.note: to lie is to remain in a place, as snow lies

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone claims the right to stay at the head of talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal claim to hold another's property until a debt is paid is a kind of right.

clue.text: Oppose United and, later, European entering formal agreement

indicators.note: the second letter goes in after the first, further along
the letter goes into the agreement

parts.note: a contract is a formal agreement
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A football club and a European side sign a deal to fight something.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes in after CO and E, 'later', after CONT.
explanation.definitionFit: To act against something to neutralise its effect is to resist or work against it.

clue.text: A small cat and a big dog

parts.note: a kit is a kitten, a young cat

explanation.surface: Pets of two sizes: a kitten and a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Japanese breed of hound.

clue.text: Exercise before game for World Cup team, perhaps

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A team warms up before a World Cup match.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American country has qualified for the football finals; 'perhaps' marks one example.

clue.text: Fuss follows despot giving away drug for every ruffian

indicators.note: the fuss comes last, following the rest
the tyrant loses some letters, giving them up

parts.note: pot is cannabis
per means for each
ado is fuss

explanation.surface: A tyrant without his drugs causes a fuss at each turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving away' strips the drug from the tyrant's word; 'follows' sends the fuss to the end even though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless outlaw of the Wild West type is a thug or ruffian.

clue.text: Tent was initially of poor quality fabric

indicators.note: only the first letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: ill can mean bad or of poor quality, as in ill-made

explanation.surface: A tent's material was shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven cloth with diagonal ribs, like denim, is a sturdy textile.

clue.text: Our hydrangea'd turned out rudely vigorous

indicators.note: the letters are turned out of their order, as soil from a pot

explanation.surface: A gardener boasts that their shrub has grown with crude energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude but effective, unpolished yet robust, describes something hasty but sturdy.
